items.claim: The narrative-zone opening holds in the bytes: the date-formula onset holds at byte tier against the source, the one parashah mark it cites is correctly placed and correctly typed outside the span, and the close stops short of the fresh royal-messenger frame that opens the next verse.
items.evidence: The row's pointed run matches its cited MT verse at BYTE tier on a fresh check against the source bytes (full verse, no degradation). The mark claim checks out at MT keys: MT 35:10 carries a PE (single-witness), it is the verse immediately preceding the span, and the type is kept unconflated with SAMEKH; it is read as closing the preceding oracle, never as a driver. Span-relevant mark symmetry holds — MT 36:1-36:3 carries no PE and no SAMEKH of its own, and the only other marks anywhere in this cluster's range are the SAMEKH at MT 36:22 and MT 36:16, both inside later rows and both disclosed there; the paseq seg at MT 36:2 is count-only and is correctly not claimed. The terminus is frame-correct in the bytes: the next verse carries כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (oshb:Isa.36.4, byte), the named human speaker's frame — one of the book's four royal-messenger koh-amar sites (MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3) against 44 divine-frame verses — so the row's close does not absorb a speech frame it does not itself carry. The only tie across 36:3|36:4 is the anaphoric אֲלֵיהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.36.4, byte) resolving to this row's three named officials: ordinary inter-sentence anaphora, not a byte-true device bracketing the seam.

items.claim: The frame-ownership call at 36:4 is right, but the row's adonai argument is false in the bytes — the courtly token it quotes is not the same form as the divine title — and it leaves the identical courtly token inside its own span and the YHWH-speech attribution at its own closing verse unengaged.
items.evidence: Both pointed runs check out at BYTE tier against their cited MT verses, and the frame call is correct: כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (oshb:Isa.36.4, byte) names the human speaker's master, one of the four royal-messenger sites (MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3). The defect is the identity claim that the quoted token is 'the same bare-adonai form that elsewhere in the book addresses the divine Adonai'. Swept object, named first: the unprefixed and unsuffixed adonai token, finals-normalized, book-wide — 44 tokens in 44 verses carry qamats under the nun (the divine title, e.g. אֲדֹנָ֛י at oshb:Isa.6.1, byte) and EXACTLY 3 tokens in 3 verses carry hiriq (MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12 — all three inside this cluster). The row's own quoted token is אֲדֹנִ֖י (oshb:Isa.36.8, byte), hiriq-pointed. The two are the same consonantal skeleton and NOT the same form; the identity the row asserts holds at SKELETON tier only, and it is asserted beside a byte-tier label with no tier named — the courtly/divine split here is visible in the pointing, not merely in the referent. Second, symmetry on the object the row itself engages: the identical courtly token recurs inside this row's own span at עַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י (oshb:Isa.36.9, byte) and is undisclosed. Third, the row's terminus verse is carried in English only, while its bytes read יְהוָה֙ אָמַ֣ר אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.10, byte) — a YHWH-speech attribution placed in the Assyrian herald's mouth at the row's own closing seam, and one the book's amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency census (52 verses; in this zone MT 37:6, 37:21, 37:33) does not carry; a row whose whole case is frame ownership owes that verse a word.

items.claim: The language handling and the doubled ketiv/qere disclosure are correct, but the row's claim that the verse repeats the courtly bare-adonai form twice over is false in the bytes: its two adonai tokens are two different forms and only one belongs to the bare-token object.
items.evidence: The pointed run checks out at BYTE tier against its cited MT verse, and three of the row's claims stand: the verse is one of the book's four doubled ketiv/qere verses (MT 26:20, 28:15, 36:12, 52:5), checked at MT keys before any slicing; the herald's title is genuinely two tokens, רַב שָׁקֵ֗ה (oshb:Isa.36.12, byte), so a single-token needle finds nothing; and the language handling is right — the neighbouring request is narrated story content, the verse's own language label is Hebrew like every verse of this book, and no Aramaic verse label is asserted. The defect is the count claim. The verse's two adonai-family tokens are אֲדֹנֶ֤יךָ and אֲדֹנִ֔י (oshb:Isa.36.12, byte): a 2ms-suffixed form and a 1cs-suffixed form. They differ at BYTE tier and also at SKELETON tier (a final kaf on the first, absent on the second), and only the second is a member of the bare-token object, which stands hiriq-pointed at exactly 3 sites book-wide (MT 36:8, 36:9, 36:12). 'The same courtly bare-adonai form, twice over' therefore doubles a count-object inside the book's largest ketiv/qere class; the zone in fact carries four distinct adonai-family forms across MT 36:8/36:9, 36:12, 37:4 and 37:6. Related: the row labels its whole run byte tier without naming which of its tokens are ketiv and which qere — the two unpointed ketiv tokens חראיהם and שיניהם (oshb:Isa.36.12, byte) stand beside their pointed qere partners צוֹאָתָ֗ם and מֵימֵ֥י רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם (oshb:Isa.36.12, byte) in that same run, and a doubled-note verse owes that naming before it counts anything in the verse.

items.claim: Frame ownership and the mid-speech parashah disclosure are exact, but the seam the row actually decides is argued in English only, and its prose substitutes 'Hebrew' for a byte term neither witness renders that way.
items.evidence: Both pointed runs check out at BYTE tier against their cited MT verses, and both frames are correctly owned: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ (oshb:Isa.36.14, byte) and כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר (oshb:Isa.36.16, byte) name the human king, giving this row two of the four royal-messenger sites (MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3) and no divine frame. The mark claim is exact — MT 36:16 carries a SAMEKH (single-witness), correctly typed, correctly disclosed as falling mid-speech and not read as a break; MT 36:13-36:20 carries no other PE or SAMEKH, so span-relevant symmetry is satisfied. Two gaps, both at the row's onset. First, the boundary driver — a herald standing, calling in a loud voice, in a named language, to a new audience — rests on the English rendering alone: the bytes are וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ רַב שָׁקֵ֔ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְקוֹל גָּד֖וֹל יְהוּדִ֑ית וַיֹּ֕אמֶר (oshb:Isa.36.13, byte) and are nowhere spliced, while both pointed runs the row does supply sit mid-span rather than at the seam being decided. Second, the row's prose says the proclamation was made 'in Hebrew rather than Aramaic'; the byte term inside that unquoted run is the Judahite-language noun, which the row's own English quotation renders 'the Jews' language'. Neither witness reads 'Hebrew' there, and in a book where every verse's own language label is Hebrew and language-labelling is a live failure class, the byte term should have carried the claim.

items.claim: The join across the chapter division is byte-supportable, but the row never quotes the catchword that supports it, never engages the one tier-3 mark inside its span that falls exactly at the junction it joins, and leaves a byte-true covering-in-sackcloth tie straddling its own closing seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: The pointed run checks out at BYTE tier against its cited MT verse, and the mark claim is exact: MT 36:22 carries a SAMEKH (single-witness), correctly typed, and it is the only PE or SAMEKH inside MT 36:21-37:1. Three problems follow. (1) That mark is keyed to MT 36:22, the verse immediately before the row's INTERNAL junction — the very join the row makes — so its one disclosed corroborating signal is in fact the weak rival to its own decision; the row discloses the mark's existence but not its bearing on its own join, and its rejected alternative argues only the other edge. Tier-3, single-witness, never a driver, and absence would never be counterevidence — but presence at the join owes an engagement. (2) The join's strongest byte warrant goes unquoted: קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.36.22, byte) is answered across the junction by וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת בְּגָדָ֑יו (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte) — the tear-and-garment pair, shared root, distinct pointed forms, so a ROOT-tier tie and not byte-identical recurrence — while the row argues 'the same participants and the same report-and-response movement' in English. (3) Against the row: the covering-in-sackcloth language crosses its OWN closing seam. וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte) is picked up immediately by מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים (oshb:Isa.37.2, byte) — the same verbal root in a different stem plus the same noun in the plural, again ROOT tier — a seam-straddling tie that argues continuity into the following unit and is nowhere disclosed.

items.claim: Both frame calls in this row are correct, but its koh-amar digit is wrong: the Assyrian king owns three prior royal-messenger sites, not two, and this cluster's own preceding rows name all three.
items.evidence: Both pointed runs check out at BYTE tier against their cited MT verses and both ownerships are right: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ (oshb:Isa.37.3, byte) carries the named Judahite king's frame and כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.37.6, byte) the divine frame, the tier-1 object. The defect is the digit. The book's royal-messenger koh-amar sites are exactly MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16 and 37:3 (4 verses against 44 divine-frame verses); of those four, the Assyrian king owns THREE — כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ הַגָּדוֹל֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר (oshb:Isa.36.4, byte), כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ (oshb:Isa.36.14, byte), כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֗וּר (oshb:Isa.36.16, byte) — and the fourth is this row's own Hezekiah frame. 'The Assyrian king's two prior sites', and equally 'both the royal-messenger sites in chapter 36', undercounts by one and contradicts the immediately preceding rows, which themselves name 36:4 as the Assyrian king's frame and 36:14/36:16 as two more. This is the one digit class this zone flags as meaningless unless the frame owner is named: the owner is named here and the digit is still wrong, which makes the 'third frame-owner' architecture claim rest on a bad census. Secondary: the row quotes the verse containing כֹּ֥ה תֹאמְר֖וּן (oshb:Isa.37.6, byte) without distinguishing that prefixed speech-commission from the counted frame that follows it three tokens later in the same verse — the exact distinction the next unit's argument turns on, with its byte anchor already inside this row.

items.claim: The row rightly refuses to inflate the koh-amar census at 37:10, but it mislabels that verse's verb form as an imperative, builds a letter-versus-in-person contrast its own span's bytes do not carry, and makes a recurrence claim with no quoted form and no tier.
items.evidence: The pointed run checks out at BYTE tier against its cited MT verse, the herald's title is indeed two tokens there, and the census refusal is correct: the verse in question opens כֹּ֣ה תֹאמְר֗וּן (oshb:Isa.37.10, byte), not a koh-amar frame, and it is absent from the book's koh-amar list (48 verses; royal-messenger MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3). Three defects. (1) Form class: the row calls that construction a plain imperative-to-speak. The bytes carry a prefixed second-person plural form with paragogic nun, not an imperative; the book's actual imperative of this verb stands inside this same cluster at אִמְרוּ נָ֖א (oshb:Isa.36.4, byte), and both witnesses part exactly there, rendering the 37:10 form as a future-modal 'you shall speak' against 36:4's plain 'tell'. With no morphology layer available, a form-class label the bytes and both renderings contest should have been held, not asserted. (2) The contrast that the message was 'sent this time by letter rather than delivered in person' has no support inside the row's own span: its bytes read וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.37.9, byte) — messengers dispatched with a speech commission — and the document noun first appears one verse past the row's close, in the plural, taken הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים וַיִּקְרָאֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Isa.37.14, byte), from the hand of those same messengers, which contradicts the contrast rather than grounding it; the singular 'letter' is the English rendering, so the argument works in the translation and not in the Hebrew. (3) The claim that this speech restates the gods-of-the-nations argument already made carries no quoted form and no tier, when the byte evidence is unusually strong: הַהִצִּ֜ילוּ אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ (oshb:Isa.36.18, byte) against הַהִצִּ֨ילוּ אוֹתָ֜ם אֱלֹהֵ֤י הַגּוֹיִם֙ (oshb:Isa.37.12, byte) share a two-token run that is BYTE-IDENTICAL at exactly two sites book-wide (MT 36:18 and MT 37:12; sweep: 2 verses), while the verb form heading each differs in accentuation; and the interrogative place-name chain אַיֵּ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י חֲמָת֙ וְאַרְפָּ֔ד אַיֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י סְפַרְוָ֑יִם (oshb:Isa.36.19, byte) against אַיֵּ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ חֲמָת֙ וּמֶ֣לֶךְ אַרְפָּ֔ד וּמֶ֖לֶךְ לָעִ֣יר סְפַרְוָ֑יִם (oshb:Isa.37.13, byte) shares a place name attested at exactly those two verses (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier). That is a byte-tier cross-row bracket the row asserts in prose without quoting or tiering it.

items.claim: The frame-plus-speech bound is defensible, but the row never splices the prayer frame its whole argument rests on and does not disclose that the following verse binds itself back to this unit's prayer by the same root.
items.evidence: Both pointed runs check out at BYTE tier against their cited MT verses, and the close is defensible on a tier-1 ground the row does not state: the next verse opens כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.37.21, byte), a divine koh-amar frame, which is a genuine seam. Two gaps. (1) The stated driver is that frame and speech stay together, but the frame verse itself is never spliced: וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ אֶל יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.37.15, byte) is the entire warrant for holding the narrated act with the prayer's content, and it is argued in English while the two pointed runs go to the span's outer edges. (2) The following verse ties itself back across the row's own closing seam: אֲשֶׁר֙ הִתְפַּלַּ֣לְתָּ אֵלַ֔י (oshb:Isa.37.21, byte) names this unit's prayer as the ground of the answering word, on the same verbal root as the unquoted frame verb — a ROOT-tier tie, not byte-identical, straddling the seam and undisclosed, and it argues continuity against the row's assertion of a self-contained rhetorical terminus. Minor, same class: the row's 'the letter' follows the English singular, while the bytes of its own opening verse read a plural noun with a singular object suffix on the reading verb in the same run, הַסְּפָרִ֛ים מִיַּ֥ד הַמַּלְאָכִ֖ים וַיִּקְרָאֵ֑הוּ (oshb:Isa.37.14, byte); and the messenger noun there is definite, resolving to the indefinite one dispatched in the preceding unit's bytes, וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Isa.37.9, byte) — a second undisclosed tie across the row's opening seam.
